intelligence.human_view: A gray flat icon is the small thing that makes a whole page look messy — one dull little shape, and the eye catches it instead of the beautiful things around it. Every icon has to be the nicest elevated, almost jewel-like icon: a real object, a ball not a flat circle. And the fix is not to design new icons for the messy page — the Personal icons are already better, already more pro — so harvest them verbatim and make no new ones. The one exception proves the rule: the three-line menu control, the way it flows, is fine as it is — the exception is named, not assumed, and it is the only one. This is the no-gray-text law (SN-3177) extended to icons: gray is never the best, anywhere, in words or in shapes.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a page full of beautiful shiny jewels, and then a few dull gray flat ones mixed in — they make the whole page look messy. Every icon should be a shiny jewel, raised up like a little ball, never flat and gray. And the best jewels already exist on the Personal page — so we take those very same ones and use them here, instead of making new ones. Only the little three-line button stays as it is, because it flows so nicely.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, the little gray flat icons are the ones making the page look messy — a dull gray shape is never the best icon anywhere. Every icon should be the nicest, raised up like a little jewel, round and real. And we already have the best ones on the Personal page, so we take those very same ones and put them here — no new ones needed. Just the one little three-line button stays as it is, the way it flows.
